description: Reviewed initial codebase files (soggfy-original) and defined the porting objective for macOS.
Configured the CMake environment and successfully compiled the baseline dylib payload using Ninja.
Executed launch.sh and inspected dyld logs using 'log show' to verify successful dylib injection.
Investigated codesign entitlements of the Spotify binary to understand and bypass hardened runtime restrictions.
Began hunting for Ogg Vorbis decoding hooks by comparing symbol maps with soggfy-original patterns.
Wrote and executed 'search_pattern.py' to scan the PatchedSpotify Mach-O binary for known byte signatures.
Continuously relaunched patched Spotify after iterative recompilations of the interception hooks.
Used radare2 (r2) to search the binary's string sections specifically for the 'OggS' magic header bytes.
Wrote and executed a heuristic ARM64 scanner 'search_refs.py' which successfully mapped relative ADRP/ADD instructions to the OggS offset.
Developed 'find_branches.py' to trace execution flows backward from the OggS references to the decoder vtables.
Ran 'patch_macho.py' to forcibly inject an LC_LOAD_DYLIB load command directly into the binary header.
Tested the headless TypeScript orchestration wrapper 'soggfy-download.ts' for the first time.
Established bidirectional IPC communication with the injected payload via the local socket '/tmp/soggfy.sock'.
Disassembled specific hook points using 'llvm-objdump' to verify instruction layout before overwriting them.
Sampled the Spotify process during a hanging playback session to identify bottleneck threads causing real-time extraction delays.
Recompiled the time-bypassing payload and forcibly killed Spotify to clear IPC deadlocks.
Edited the Spotify 'prefs' file to enforce 'audio.play_bitrate=2' for max quality streaming.
Discovered that the extracted audio files contained intermittent blocks of silence and corruption.
Wrote and ran 'verify_silence.sh' to programmatically quantify the silence corruption bug across different tracks.
Examined the 'AudioConverterFillComplexBuffer' and underrun flags in the C++ hooking logic to trace dropped chunks.
Used 'ffprobe' to check durations of malformed extraction outputs, realizing the stream was seeking out-of-order.
Verified the IPC socket pool logic, confirming the server could maintain persistent instances: 'Pool is online and ready'.
Implemented API timeout handler for hanging audio streams to gracefully terminate stuck ripping sessions.
Adjusted 'limitBytes' in 'StateManager.cpp' to ensure absolute offset mapping didn't result in buffer overflows.
Developed fully headless HTTP API routes for 'soggfy-server.ts', replacing CLI manual execution.
Investigated payload logs after encountering injected advertisements corrupting the audio file streams.
Explored and implemented 'getaddrinfo' network hooks to neutralize DNS resolution for known ad-serving domains.
Refined the injection script to utilize 'DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES' alongside 'SOGGFY_HIDDEN=0' env vars.
Committed the massive C++ refactor: offset-aware architecture, DNS ad-blocking, and dynamic API complete.
Cleaned up the workspace, deleting obsolete reverse engineering scripts (disasm, dump_flags, etc).
Performed end-to-end verification of 'soggfy-server' API endpoints while it orchestrated background Spotify instances.
Documented the highly specific 'from scratch' patching instructions in the project README.
Reversed the Spotify Web Player token endpoint to fetch access tokens needed for playlist metadata.
Initialized the React and Shadcn webapp frontend within the repository.
Finalized the project by committing the integrated web frontend and reorganizing the repository structure.
